summary: Join our Designing Customer Journeys for Impact training to master the art of crafting meaningful customer experiences that lead to lasting business success.
lede: Designing customer journeys for impact gives professionals a practical way to understand and intentionally improve how customers, beneficiaries, or citizens experience an organization. You will learn to identify personas, map end-to-end journeys, uncover pain points and moments that matter, and design clearer, more effective experiences. The course connects journey design to outcomes such as satisfaction, adoption, retention, compliance, and social impact. Through hands-on visual tools and simple frameworks, you will learn to communicate improved journeys and inspire stakeholder action across corporate, public, and NGO environments.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who regularly shape, manage, or influence customer and stakeholder experiences. This course is designed for: Customer experience (CX) managers and specialists. Service delivery and operations managers. Marketing and communications professionals responsible for engagement. Product and service owners in digital or physical channels. Public sector staff improving citizen or service delivery journeys. NGO and program managers designing beneficiary or partner journeys. Call center, frontline, or branch managers wanting to reduce friction. Strategy and transformation leads working on customer-centric initiatives. Business analysts and designers involved in process and service redesign. Anyone who needs to understand and redesign end-to-end customer journeys for better impact.
modules: Identifying Pain Points and Moments of Truth
Designing Journeys for Impact and Experience
Using Data and Feedback to Improve Journeys
Prioritizing Improvements and Building the Case for Change
Embedding Customer Journey Thinking in Culture and Practice
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of customer service principles and some experience in customer-facing roles or projects.
